<feature feature-id="CC-0061">
  <title>Add govulncheck job to CI for Go vulnerability scanning</title>
  <description># GitHub Issue #144: Add govulncheck job to CI for Go vulnerability scanning

**Category**: security | **Scope**: Small

**Description**: There is no static security analysis for Go dependencies in the CI pipeline. `govulncheck` is the official Go vulnerability scanner maintained by the Go team and detects actually reachable vulnerable code paths — not just dependency list matches. A new CI job should be added to `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` that runs `govulncheck` against all Go modules whenever Go source changes are detected.

Proposed job:

```yaml
govulncheck:
  needs: [changes]
  if: needs.changes.outputs.go == 'true'
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  timeout-minutes: 10
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
      with:
        go-version-file: go.work
    - run: go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest
    - run: |
        govulncheck ./internal/common/...
        govulncheck ./operators/keystone/...
        govulncheck ./operators/c5c3/...
```

**Motivation**: Container images are already scanned for vulnerabilities (Grype in the existing CI), but the Go source code itself is not. A supply-chain vulnerability in a transitive Go dependency would only surface during the container image scan — too late in the development lifecycle. Shifting this check left into the CI pipeline catches known vulnerabilities at the pull request stage, before images are even built.

**Affected Areas**:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yaml`

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] New `govulncheck` job in `ci.yaml` gated on `needs.changes.outputs.go == 'true'`
- [ ] Job runs `govulncheck` against all Go module paths (`internal/common`, `operators/keystone`, `operators/c5c3`)
- [ ] Job fails the pipeline when a reachable vulnerability is detected
- [ ] Job is added to any branch protection required-checks if applicable
- [ ] Existing CI jobs are not affected

**Labels:** enhancement

---
Source: https://github.com/C5C3/forge/issues/144</description>

  <implementation-notes>**Architecture:** The govulncheck job is a standalone conditional job, structurally identical to `test-race`. It depends only on the `changes` job and is NOT in the gate chain for E2E or publish jobs. This matches the existing CI DAG pattern where informational Go checks run in parallel without blocking the critical path.

**Placement:** Insert after `test-race` (line ~257) and before `verify-codegen` (line ~258) in ci.yaml. Both are Go-focused checks; govulncheck fits logically between them.

**govulncheck @latest:** Unlike other pinned tools (controller-gen, gofumpt), govulncheck uses `@latest` intentionally. The Go team recommends this because govulncheck's vulnerability database is updated frequently, and pinning to an old version defeats the purpose of vulnerability scanning. This is a deliberate deviation from CC-0018 pinning policy, justified by the security tool's nature.

**Fail-fast behavior:** The three `govulncheck` invocations run sequentially in a single `run:` block. GitHub Actions uses `bash -eo pipefail` by default, so the first module with a reachable vulnerability will fail the job immediately. This is acceptable — you need to fix all vulnerabilities regardless, and fail-fast provides faster feedback.

**Module path maintenance:** When a new Go module is added to `go.work`, the govulncheck step must also be updated with the new module path. This is similar to how the `test` job matrix (`[common, keystone, c5c3]`) must be updated for new modules.

**Key files:**
- `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` — the single workflow file to modify
- `go.work` — defines the three Go modules to scan (source of truth for module paths)
- `docs/reference/ci-workflow.md` — reference documentation to update
- `hack/ci-resolve-changes.sh` — resolves `go` output from path-filter (not modified, but explains gating)
- `.grype.yaml` — existing container vulnerability scanner config (separate concern, not modified)</implementation-notes>
</feature>
